findings.actual: The scheme-less text is accepted and saved. findings.name: New dashboard with a spaces-only name shows a raw validation string and renames the button to \"Failed\"
findings.summary: The save is refused with a raw schema message under the field — \"Value must be a non-blank string.\" — and the primary button's label changes from \"Create\" to \"Failed\" and stays that way. Nothing tells the person in plain words that the name may not be blank or only spaces, and the button now reads like a status rather than an action. The POST /api/dashboard returns 400 and two console errors are logged. (on /collection/root (New → Dashboard dialog))
findings.expected: The Create button stays disabled for a blank/whitespace-only name, or the dialog refuses it with a plain message such as \"Name can't be blank\", and the button keeps its label so the person can correct the name and try again.
findings.actual: The save is refused with a raw schema message under the field — \"Value must be a non-blank string.\" — and the primary button's label changes from \"Create\" to \"Failed\" and stays that way. Nothing tells the person in plain words that the name may not be blank or only spaces, and the button now reads like a status rather than an action. The POST /api/dashboard returns 400 and two console errors are logged.
reproSteps: Sign in with eval@momentic.ai / momentic-eval-1.
On /collection/root click "New" in the top bar, then "Dashboard" in the menu.
Type three spaces into the Name field of the "New dashboard" dialog and click "Create".

findings.name: Saving a stale second tab silently deletes a card added in the other tab, with no conflict warning
findings.summary: Saving from the stale tab overwrote the dashboard with its old copy: the text card "agent14-evidence-card-from-tab2" added and saved from the other tab disappeared, and the dashboard kept only the heading added from the stale tab. No conflict warning, no confirmation dialog and no error appeared in either tab; the stale tab reported a normal successful save. Reloading the other tab shows the lost card is really gone from the server. The same happened on a first run with the dashboard title: tab 2 renamed it and saved, then tab 1 (opened before that rename) saved its own older state and silently put the old title back. (on /dashboard/14-agent14-persist)
findings.expected: When the dashboard has been changed by the other tab since the stale tab loaded it, saving in the stale tab should notice the newer version and warn (for example "This dashboard was changed by someone else"), instead of silently discarding the other tab's card.
findings.actual: Saving from the stale tab overwrote the dashboard with its old copy: the text card "agent14-evidence-card-from-tab2" added and saved from the other tab disappeared, and the dashboard kept only the heading added from the stale tab. No conflict warning, no confirmation dialog and no error appeared in either tab; the stale tab reported a normal successful save. Reloading the other tab shows the lost card is really gone from the server. The same happened on a first run with the dashboard title: tab 2 renamed it and saved, then tab 1 (opened before that rename) saved its own older state and silently put the old title back.
reproSteps: Open /dashboard/14-agent14-persist (dashboard named "agent14-persist", with a "Release requests" card) in two browser tabs of the same signed-in session.
In the first tab click the pencil "Edit dashboard" button and leave that tab open in edit mode without saving.

In the second tab click the pencil "Edit dashboard", click the T ("Add a heading or text box") button, choose "Text", type "agent14-evidence-card-from-tab2" and click "Save". The text card is on the dashboard.
Go back to the first (stale) tab, which still shows the dashboard without that text card, click the T button, choose "Heading", type "agent14-evidence-heading-tab1" and click "Save".
Look at the saved dashboard in the first tab, then reload the second tab.

findings.expected: When the save cannot be authenticated, the person is told the change was not saved (an error message or a redirect to the sign-in page). The unsaved edit is not silently discarded behind a blank page.
findings.actual: The save request (PUT /api/dashboard/6) was answered 401 Unauthenticated and the whole app went to a blank white page (title still \"Metabase\"): no error message, no redirect to the sign-in form, no notice that the edit was not saved. After reloading and signing in again the dashboard still showed the old text card, so the edit was silently lost. The console logged \"Request entities,dashboards,6,update failed: {status: 401, data: Unauthenticated}\".
reproSteps: Sign in as eval@momentic.ai / momentic-eval-1 and open the dashboard /dashboard/6-agent11-dash (my own dashboard, one heading card and one text card).

findings.name: The only tab of a dashboard cannot be renamed: its menu offers only "Duplicate" while every tab of a multi-tab dashboard offers "Rename"
findings.summary: With only one tab, the tab's chevron menu holds just \"Duplicate\" — no \"Rename\" (and no Delete) — and clicking/double-clicking the tab name does not open an editor either, so the tab keeps the name \"Tab 1\" for good. As soon as a second tab exists the same menu shows Rename / Duplicate / Delete, so renaming is only available when there are two or more tabs. (on /dashboard/17-agent13-responsive-dashboard#edit)
findings.expected: The tab menu offers \"Rename\" for the dashboard's only tab too (as it does for every tab when there are two or more), so a dashboard with a single tab can be given a meaningful tab name.
findings.actual: With only one tab, the tab's chevron menu holds just \"Duplicate\" — no \"Rename\" (and no Delete) — and clicking/double-clicking the tab name does not open an editor either, so the tab keeps the name \"Tab 1\" for good. As soon as a second tab exists the same menu shows Rename / Duplicate / Delete, so renaming is only available when there are two or more tabs.
reproSteps: Sign in with eval@momentic.ai / momentic-eval-1 and open /dashboard/17-agent13-responsive-dashboard.
Click the pencil "Edit dashboard" button, then delete every tab but the first one (each remaining tab's chevron > Delete) so the tab bar shows only "Tab 1".
Click the small chevron-down right of "Tab 1" and read the menu: it contains only "Duplicate".
Click the text "Tab 1" itself (once and double-click): nothing becomes editable.
Now click the "+" at the end of the tab bar to add a second tab and open that new tab's chevron: the menu now contains Rename, Duplicate and Delete.
